48-year-old man whose cardiology clinic notes (most recently 2026-06-12) document paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; the chart also carries 'other specified cardiac dysrhythmias' and prior long-term anticoagulant use. Only famotidine and pantoprazole are current, so no anticoagulant is in place. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure - congestive heart failure unspecified, acute systolic heart failure and other primary cardiomyopathies documented in the chart - 1, plus hypertension 1). A score of 2 or more in a man meets the guideline recommendation for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of anticoagulation needs review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 2026-08-20 (valid through 2026-12-28) and is current. The 2026-08-12 summary of outside records documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 and 2 units transfused, and states that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. The clinic restarted apixaban (and continued aspirin plus clopidogrel) at the 2026-08-20 visit without any documented reconsideration of that recommendation. A current anticoagulant despite a documented recent major GI bleed and an explicit instruction to hold pending review needs prescriber review.

At the 2026-07-15 cardiology visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started. Rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was ordered at the same visit and was never stopped: both orders are active as of 2026-09-24 (rivaroxaban valid to 2026-12-25, apixaban to 2026-12-26) and the 2026-07-15 medication list itself shows both drugs. Two concurrent oral anticoagulants create a major bleeding hazard, particularly in a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and thrombocytopenia. Needs immediate reconciliation.

The 2026-06-10 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm with no consistent P waves at a ventricular rate of about 140/min, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same atrial fibrillation with a rate of about 144/min. The documented rhythm and rate are therefore both inconsistent with the same-day tracings, and the discrepancy needs clinical review (this patient is on warfarin for pulmonary embolism, and unrecognised rapid AF changes rate-control and anticoagulation decisions).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) is current, most recently ordered 2026-04-23 and valid through 2027-01-02. The patient's most recent ECG is 108018814 (2023-10-08): sinus rhythm at 68/min, RR 0.88 s, QT about 480 ms, Bazett QTc about 512 ms, which meets the clinic threshold of 500 ms or more and requires prescriber review. Note that the 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this same tracing as 'QT acceptable'. Most recent electrolytes are potassium 4.1 mmol/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 2025-08-23), so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. A repeat ECG on therapy plus review of the need for escitalopram is required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is current, most recently ordered 2026-07-29 and valid through 2027-01-05. The most recent ECG is 106885519 (2025-11-24), obtained two weeks after amiodarone was started: sinus rhythm at 62/min, RR 0.96 s, QT about 520 ms, Bazett QTc about 529 ms, at or above the clinic 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.4 mmol/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (2026-04-20) are normal, so the prolongation is drug related. The patient is also on warfarin, so any amiodarone dose change will need INR follow-up. Prescriber review of continued amiodarone and a repeat ECG are required.

interpretations.explanation: Recorded at the 2026-03-07 cardiology visit, 5 days after citalopram was started. Regular P wave before every QRS with an upright P in II and a normal PR; RR 0.66-0.86 s with mild respiratory variation. Narrow QRS, normal precordial progression, no bundle branch block and no AV block. QT 330 ms at RR 0.74 s gives a Bazett QTc of 382 ms, well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. No prior tracing for comparison. The note for that visit describing 'sinus rhythm' agrees with the tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular RR 0.57-0.59 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS and PR about 194 ms (upper normal). QRS 98 ms - slightly prolonged but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block is coded; the ST-T complex is broad and the repolarisation abnormal. QT about 323 ms at RR 0.58 s gives QTc 424 ms. The previous tracing 100698634 (2025-06-20) showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with QTc 388 ms; the rate has fallen but rhythm, conduction and QTc are otherwise unchanged (QTc change 36 ms, below the 60 ms threshold).

Sinus tachycardia at 109/min. The RR intervals are regular (0.54-0.62 s, coefficient of variation 0.03) and a low amplitude P wave precedes each QRS with PR about 136 ms; the baseline is noisy, which reduces beat-to-beat P wave correlation, but the rhythm is regular and atrially driven. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +45 degrees. QT 321 ms at RR 0.55 s gives QTc 433 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: RR intervals range from 0.35 to 0.65 s and are irregularly irregular (coefficient of variation 0.16), with no organised atrial activity before the QRS complexes (pre-QRS beat-to-beat correlation 0.40, no measurable P wave), so no PR interval can be given. Mean ventricular rate about 144/min. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about -2 degrees. QT 289 ms at a median RR of 0.42 s gives QTc 447 ms. The preceding tracing 107914094, taken 2 hours earlier the same day, shows the same atrial fibrillation at about 140/min, so there is no change between them. Both tracings contradict the 2026-06-10 clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'.

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular RR 0.86-0.88 s, consistent P waves with PR 152 ms. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis -24 degrees, within the normal range. QT 406 ms at RR 0.87 s gives QTc 435 ms. The previous tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27, sinus 60/min, QTc 402 ms) shows the same rhythm and conduction; the QTc change of 33 ms is below the 60 ms threshold, so there are no coded changes.

Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular RR 0.60-0.63 s, with a small upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and a short PR of about 100-105 ms. QRS 74 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis -12 degrees. QT 294 ms at RR 0.62 s gives QTc 375 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular RR 0.82-0.84 s, consistent P waves with PR 138 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block, axis +22 degrees. QT 373 ms at RR 0.83 s gives QTc 409 ms, below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. This is the only ECG in the chart and it predates the start of escitalopram on 2026-08-01, so no prior comparison is possible and a post-start tracing is still required.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.70, 1.13, 1.15, 1.17, 0.74, 0.91, 0.70 s; coefficient of variation 0.20) and no organised P wave can be identified before the QRS complexes (pre-QRS amplitude 0.024 mV with beat-to-beat correlation only 0.63), so no PR interval is reported. Mean ventricular rate about 53/min. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +25 degrees. QT 442 ms at a median RR of 1.13 s gives QTc 415 ms. The previous tracing 107873952, only three days earlier (2024-11-12), showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with a clear P wave and PR 176 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation. The patient is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min, regular RR 0.98-1.08 s, with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and a short PR of about 94 ms. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +59 degrees. QT 429 ms at RR 1.04 s gives QTc 423 ms. The previous tracing 106045460 from the day before (2025-03-08, sinus 62/min, PR 96 ms, QTc 455 ms) is essentially the same; the QTc change of 32 ms is below the 60 ms threshold. Note that this tracing long predates the haloperidol started on 2026-09-15, for which a new ECG is due.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular RR 0.72-0.73 s, consistent P waves with PR 140 ms. QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block, axis +51 degrees. QT 343 ms at RR 0.72 s gives QTc 404 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77/min, regular RR 0.77-0.80 s, with a prominent consistent P wave and PR 154 ms. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +64 degrees. QT 399 ms at RR 0.78 s gives QTc 451 ms. The previous tracing 109048192 (2020-02-02) was also sinus at 75/min but with a much longer QT, giving a QTc of about 528 ms; the QTc has therefore fallen by more than 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min with a consistent P wave preceding each QRS (P wave consistency 0.97) and regular RR intervals of 0.50 s. Narrow QRS at 92 ms, no bundle branch block, PR 192 ms is at the upper limit of normal but not first degree block. QT 285 ms with RR 0.50 s gives QTc 403 ms. Compared with the previous tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 94 ms, QTc 398 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus bradycardia at 54/min, regular RR 1.07-1.12 s, with a consistent P wave before every QRS. The PR interval is prolonged at about 214 ms, i.e. first degree AV block, with 1:1 conduction. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +13 degrees. QT 396 ms at RR 1.11 s gives QTc 378 ms. The previous tracing 103042067 (2024-11-30, sinus 51/min, PR about 188 ms, QTc 359 ms) showed the same rhythm and no bundle branch block; PR has lengthened slightly but none of the coded change categories apply (QTc change 19 ms).

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. RR intervals vary chaotically from 0.29 to 0.58 s (coefficient of variation 0.19) with no reproducible atrial deflection before the QRS complexes (pre-QRS beat-to-beat correlation 0.17), so no PR interval can be measured. Mean ventricular rate about 153/min. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -16 degrees. QT 258 ms at a median RR of 0.39 s gives QTc 413 ms. The previous tracing 107374881 from the evening before (2025-09-12) showed a regular sinus rhythm at about 77/min (RR 0.77-0.79 s) with a single premature beat, so this tracing represents new atrial fibrillation; amiodarone was started the same morning and the patient is now on apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at 73/min, RR 0.79-0.92 s, with a prominent consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 168 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +9 degrees. QT 358 ms at RR 0.83 s gives QTc 396 ms. The previous tracing 105362569 (2025-11-21, sinus 67/min) had a QT of about 499 ms and a QTc of about 529 ms, so the QTc has decreased by more than 60 ms. The 2025-11-23 note describing 'ECG today: sinus rhythm' is consistent with this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular RR 0.80-0.82 s, with a clear P wave before each QRS and PR about 184 ms (upper normal, not first degree block). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +57 degrees. QT 377 ms at RR 0.81 s gives QTc 419 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular RR 0.86-0.90 s with a consistent upright P wave and normal PR. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +46 degrees. The T waves are broad and late: QT is about 480 ms and, at RR 0.88 s, the Bazett QTc is about 512 ms (tangent method, consistent across leads I, II, V2-V6), i.e. above the 500 ms clinic threshold. The previous tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23) had QTc 357 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. This patient is on escitalopram, and the 2024-05-14 note that started it described this tracing as 'QT acceptable'; the measured QTc does not support that.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 0.49-0.50 s and perfectly regular, with a low amplitude but consistent P wave before every QRS. PR 172 ms, QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +59 degrees. QT 281 ms at RR 0.50 s gives QTc 399 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 101/min with regular RR intervals and a clear P wave before each QRS (PR 132 ms). QRS 90 ms with normal precordial progression and no conduction block; axis +58 degrees. QT 312 ms at RR 0.59 s gives QTc 405 ms. The immediately preceding tracing 102910502 was taken 34 seconds earlier on the same day and is essentially identical (sinus 101/min, QRS 90 ms, QTc 401 ms), so there are no changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, RR 1.14-1.18 s and regular, with a small but consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 166 ms. QRS 92 ms; large precordial voltages with deep S in V1 and tall R in V6, but no bundle branch block. Axis +34 degrees. QT 431 ms at RR 1.16 s gives QTc 400 ms. Compared with 104629882 (2023-05-22, sinus 57/min with an occasional premature beat, QTc 369 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (change 31 ms).

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 0.49-0.50 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 132 ms). The QRS is now narrow at 82 ms. QRS voltages are low; the net QRS is negative in I and aVL and slightly positive in aVF, giving a frontal axis of about +175 degrees (rightward). QT 293 ms at RR 0.50 s gives QTc 416 ms. The previous tracing 106516875, recorded 13 hours earlier the same day, had a markedly wide QRS of 152 ms with a tall broad R wave in V1 and a wide terminal negativity in I and V6, i.e. a right bundle branch block pattern; that wide QRS has resolved on the present tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular RR 0.94-0.98 s, consistent P waves with PR 174 ms. QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +66 degrees. The QT is markedly prolonged at about 520 ms and, at RR 0.96 s, the Bazett QTc is about 529 ms (tight agreement across leads), above the 500 ms watch-list threshold. This tracing was obtained on 2025-11-24, two weeks after amiodarone was started. The previous ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07, sinus bradycardia 47/min) had a QTc of 404 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms since amiodarone was begun.

Atrial fibrillation: the ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR 0.41-1.07 s, coefficient of variation 0.28) and there is no reproducible atrial deflection before the QRS complexes (beat-to-beat correlation of the pre-QRS segment only 0.03), so no PR interval can be measured. Mean ventricular rate about 99/min. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis -51 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 327 ms at a median RR of 0.61 s gives QTc 420 ms. This is the only tracing in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison. The patient carries a diagnosis of atrial fibrillation and is anticoagulated with warfarin.

arguments.explanation: Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, RR 0.54 s and perfectly regular, with a clear consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 164 ms - no evidence of atrial flutter despite the coded history of flutter. QRS 94 ms; deep S in V1 and tall R in V6 but no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees. QT 274 ms at RR 0.54 s gives QTc 374 ms. The previous tracing 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus tachycardia 115/min, QTc 383 ms) is unchanged in rhythm, conduction and QTc.

items.explanation: 71-year-old woman with documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition I48.0). No anticoagulant is current: the only active clinic orders as of 2026-09-24 are carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine, and no note lists an anticoagulant. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior cerebral infarction/TIA 2, female 1), well above the threshold at which the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. Her most recent ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with an isolated premature beat, which does not change the need for anticoagulation in paroxysmal AF. Needs review for initiation of oral anticoagulation.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) is current, most recently ordered 2026-05-29 and valid through 2026-12-25; 40 mg is also above the 20 mg maximum advised where QT prolongation is a concern. The most recent ECG is 104821039 (2023-11-10): sinus rhythm at 70/min, RR 0.86 s, QT about 488 ms, Bazett QTc about 528 ms, above the clinic 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.5 mmol/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. Prescriber review of the citalopram dose and a current ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) has been continuous since 2022 and is current, most recently ordered 2026-08-22 and valid through 2027-01-05. The most recent ECG is 101515306 (2022-04-27): sinus rhythm at 58/min, RR 1.03 s, QT about 540 ms, Bazett QTc about 529 ms, above the clinic 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.1 mmol/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2026-02-14); magnesium is at the low end of normal and worth repleting. This 95-year-old woman is also on warfarin and metoprolol; prescriber review of continued amiodarone and an up-to-date ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10. That start date is on or after 1 September 2025 and before 1 March 2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met within the required time. (The QTc on that tracing is 529 ms, which is handled as a separate QT safety item.)

Because the start is on or after 1 March 2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was completed within the required time (sinus rhythm, QTc 382 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12. The start is before 1 March 2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo still applies (the 3/1/2026 revision explicitly leaves earlier starts on the 30-day window) and an ECG was due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was completed in time (sinus rhythm, QTc 378 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10. The start is on or after 1 March 2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded on 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, and no ECG was obtained by the due date. The requirement was therefore not met in time and is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (it is absent from the 2026-06-24 medication list and present from 2026-08-01). The start is after 1 March 2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, which predates the drug start; no ECG has been obtained since. The requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10. The start is after 1 March 2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists for this patient in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing falls inside the 14-day window and, if obtained, would satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15. The start is after 1 March 2026, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been recorded since the start (the most recent tracings are 106045460 and 104253928 from March 2025), but the due date is after the 2026-09-24 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due. It should be tracked to ensure the ECG is obtained by 2026-09-29.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01, Dr Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was completed within the required time.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (Condition 427.31, also carried in every clinic note). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery as vascular disease 1); for a man a score of 2 or more carries a guideline recommendation for oral anticoagulation. The historical code 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is remote and is not documented as an active bleeding contraindication. Needs review for initiation of oral anticoagulation.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist documented a home INR of 3.4 and decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per the anticoagulation protocol; the standing order of 2024-06-01 permits clinic pharmacists to make such changes, so this is a qualifying dose change. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since. The requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old woman on warfarin plus amiodarone.

INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was completed within the required time.

The historical code 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is remote and is not documented as an active bleeding contraindication. Needs review for initiation of oral anticoagulation.

80-year-old woman whose cardiology clinic notes (most recently 2026-05-28) document persistent atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: congestive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure) 1, hypertension 1, age 75 or older 2, type 2 diabetes mellitus 1, prior cerebral infarction/TIA with residual deficits 2, vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis) 1, female sex 1. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure - congestive heart failure unspecified, acute systolic heart failure and other primary cardiomyopathies documented in the chart - 1, plus hypertension 1). A score of 2 or more in a man meets the guideline recommendation for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of anticoagulation needs review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 2026-08-20 (valid through 2026-12-28) and is current. The clinic restarted apixaban (and continued aspirin plus clopidogrel) at the 2026-08-20 visit without any documented reconsideration of that recommendation. A current anticoagulant despite a documented recent major GI bleed and an explicit instruction to hold pending review needs prescriber review.

At the 2026-07-15 cardiology visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started. Two concurrent oral anticoagulants create a major bleeding hazard, particularly in a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and thrombocytopenia. Needs immediate reconciliation.

Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm with no consistent P waves at a ventricular rate of about 140/min, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same atrial fibrillation with a rate of about 144/min. The documented rhythm and rate are therefore both inconsistent with the same-day tracings, and the discrepancy needs clinical review (this patient is on warfarin for pulmonary embolism, and unrecognised rapid AF changes rate-control and anticoagulation decisions).

A repeat ECG on therapy plus review of the need for escitalopram is required.

Two concurrent oral anticoagulants create a major bleeding hazard, particularly in a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and thrombocytopenia. Needs immediate reconciliation.

The 2026-06-10 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm with no consistent P waves at a ventricular rate of about 140/min, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same atrial fibrillation with a rate of about 144/min. The documented rhythm and rate are therefore both inconsistent with the same-day tracings, and the discrepancy needs clinical review (this patient is on warfarin for pulmonary embolism, and unrecognised rapid AF changes rate-control and anticoagulation decisions).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) is current, most recently ordered 2026-04-23 and valid through 2027-01-02. interpretations.explanation: Recorded at the 2026-03-07 cardiology visit, 5 days after citalopram was started. Regular P wave before every QRS with an upright P in II and a normal PR; RR 0.66-0.86 s with mild respiratory variation. Narrow QRS, normal precordial progression, no bundle branch block and no AV block. QT 330 ms at RR 0.74 s gives a Bazett QTc of 382 ms, well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. No prior tracing for comparison. The note for that visit describing 'sinus rhythm' agrees with the tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular RR 0.57-0.59 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS and PR about 194 ms (upper normal). QRS 98 ms - slightly prolonged but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block is coded; the ST-T complex is broad and the repolarisation abnormal. QT about 323 ms at RR 0.58 s gives QTc 424 ms. The previous tracing 100698634 (2025-06-20) showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with QTc 388 ms; the rate has fallen but rhythm, conduction and QTc are otherwise unchanged (QTc change 36 ms, below the 60 ms threshold).

Sinus tachycardia at 109/min. The RR intervals are regular (0.54-0.62 s, coefficient of variation 0.03) and a low amplitude P wave precedes each QRS with PR about 136 ms; the baseline is noisy, which reduces beat-to-beat P wave correlation, but the rhythm is regular and atrially driven. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +45 degrees. QT 321 ms at RR 0.55 s gives QTc 433 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: RR intervals range from 0.35 to 0.65 s and are irregularly irregular (coefficient of variation 0.16), with no organised atrial activity before the QRS complexes (pre-QRS beat-to-beat correlation 0.40, no measurable P wave), so no PR interval can be given. Mean ventricular rate about 144/min. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about -2 degrees. QT 289 ms at a median RR of 0.42 s gives QTc 447 ms. The preceding tracing 107914094, taken 2 hours earlier the same day, shows the same atrial fibrillation at about 140/min, so there is no change between them. Both tracings contradict the 2026-06-10 clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'.

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular RR 0.86-0.88 s, consistent P waves with PR 152 ms. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis -24 degrees, within the normal range. QT 406 ms at RR 0.87 s gives QTc 435 ms. The previous tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27, sinus 60/min, QTc 402 ms) shows the same rhythm and conduction; the QTc change of 33 ms is below the 60 ms threshold, so there are no coded changes.

Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular RR 0.60-0.63 s, with a small upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and a short PR of about 100-105 ms. QRS 74 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis -12 degrees. QT 294 ms at RR 0.62 s gives QTc 375 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular RR 0.82-0.84 s, consistent P waves with PR 138 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block, axis +22 degrees. This is the only ECG in the chart and it predates the start of escitalopram on 2026-08-01, so no prior comparison is possible and a post-start tracing is still required.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.70, 1.13, 1.15, 1.17, 0.74, 0.91, 0.70 s; coefficient of variation 0.20) and no organised P wave can be identified before the QRS complexes (pre-QRS amplitude 0.024 mV with beat-to-beat correlation only 0.63), so no PR interval is reported. The previous tracing 107873952, only three days earlier (2024-11-12), showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with a clear P wave and PR 176 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation. The patient is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min, regular RR 0.98-1.08 s, with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and a short PR of about 94 ms. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +59 degrees. QT 429 ms at RR 1.04 s gives QTc 423 ms. The previous tracing 106045460 from the day before (2025-03-08, sinus 62/min, PR 96 ms, QTc 455 ms) is essentially the same; the QTc change of 32 ms is below the 60 ms threshold. Note that this tracing long predates the haloperidol started on 2026-09-15, for which a new ECG is due.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular RR 0.72-0.73 s, consistent P waves with PR 140 ms. QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block, axis +51 degrees. QT 343 ms at RR 0.72 s gives QTc 404 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77/min, regular RR 0.77-0.80 s, with a prominent consistent P wave and PR 154 ms. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +64 degrees. QT 399 ms at RR 0.78 s gives QTc 451 ms. The previous tracing 109048192 (2020-02-02) was also sinus at 75/min but with a much longer QT, giving a QTc of about 528 ms; the QTc has therefore fallen by more than 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min with a consistent P wave preceding each QRS (P wave consistency 0.97) and regular RR intervals of 0.50 s. Narrow QRS at 92 ms, no bundle branch block, PR 192 ms is at the upper limit of normal but not first degree block. QT 285 ms with RR 0.50 s gives QTc 403 ms. Compared with the previous tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 94 ms, QTc 398 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus bradycardia at 54/min, regular RR 1.07-1.12 s, with a consistent P wave before every QRS. The PR interval is prolonged at about 214 ms, i.e. first degree AV block, with 1:1 conduction. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +13 degrees. QT 396 ms at RR 1.11 s gives QTc 378 ms. The previous tracing 103042067 (2024-11-30, sinus 51/min, PR about 188 ms, QTc 359 ms) showed the same rhythm and no bundle branch block; PR has lengthened slightly but none of the coded change categories apply (QTc change 19 ms).

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. RR intervals vary chaotically from 0.29 to 0.58 s (coefficient of variation 0.19) with no reproducible atrial deflection before the QRS complexes (pre-QRS beat-to-beat correlation 0.17), so no PR interval can be measured. Mean ventricular rate about 153/min. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -16 degrees. QT 258 ms at a median RR of 0.39 s gives QTc 413 ms. The previous tracing 107374881 from the evening before (2025-09-12) showed a regular sinus rhythm at about 77/min (RR 0.77-0.79 s) with a single premature beat, so this tracing represents new atrial fibrillation; amiodarone was started the same morning and the patient is now on apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at 73/min, RR 0.79-0.92 s, with a prominent consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 168 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +9 degrees. QT 358 ms at RR 0.83 s gives QTc 396 ms. The previous tracing 105362569 (2025-11-21, sinus 67/min) had a QT of about 499 ms and a QTc of about 529 ms, so the QTc has decreased by more than 60 ms. The 2025-11-23 note describing 'ECG today: sinus rhythm' is consistent with this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular RR 0.80-0.82 s, with a clear P wave before each QRS and PR about 184 ms (upper normal, not first degree block). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +57 degrees. QT 377 ms at RR 0.81 s gives QTc 419 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, RR 0.54 s and perfectly regular, with a clear consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 164 ms - no evidence of atrial flutter despite the coded history of flutter. QRS 94 ms; deep S in V1 and tall R in V6 but no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees. QT 274 ms at RR 0.54 s gives QTc 374 ms. The previous tracing 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus tachycardia 115/min, QTc 383 ms) is unchanged in rhythm, conduction and QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 61/min with a single premature beat: RR intervals are 0.98, 0.99, 0.54 (premature), 1.39 (post-extrasystolic pause), then 0.98, 0.97, 0.95, 0.96, 0.98 s, and a consistent P wave precedes the sinus beats (beat-to-beat correlation 0.94). The underlying rhythm is therefore sinus, not atrial fibrillation, although the chart documents paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. PR about 200 ms, at the upper limit of normal. QRS 102 ms - mildly prolonged but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block is coded. Frontal axis -31 degrees, i.e. borderline left axis deviation. QT 365 ms at a median RR of 0.97 s gives QTc 370 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular RR 0.86-0.90 s with a consistent upright P wave and normal PR. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +46 degrees. The T waves are broad and late: QT is about 480 ms and, at RR 0.88 s, the Bazett QTc is about 512 ms (tangent method, consistent across leads I, II, V2-V6), i.e. above the 500 ms clinic threshold. The previous tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23) had QTc 357 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. This patient is on escitalopram, and the 2024-05-14 note that started it described this tracing as 'QT acceptable'; the measured QTc does not support that.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 0.49-0.50 s and perfectly regular, with a low amplitude but consistent P wave before every QRS. PR 172 ms, QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +59 degrees. QT 281 ms at RR 0.50 s gives QTc 399 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 101/min with regular RR intervals and a clear P wave before each QRS (PR 132 ms). QRS 90 ms with normal precordial progression and no conduction block; axis +58 degrees. QT 312 ms at RR 0.59 s gives QTc 405 ms. The immediately preceding tracing 102910502 was taken 34 seconds earlier on the same day and is essentially identical (sinus 101/min, QRS 90 ms, QTc 401 ms), so there are no changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, RR 1.14-1.18 s and regular, with a small but consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 166 ms. QRS 92 ms; large precordial voltages with deep S in V1 and tall R in V6, but no bundle branch block. Axis +34 degrees. QT 431 ms at RR 1.16 s gives QTc 400 ms. Compared with 104629882 (2023-05-22, sinus 57/min with an occasional premature beat, QTc 369 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (change 31 ms).

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 0.49-0.50 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 132 ms). The QRS is now narrow at 82 ms. QRS voltages are low; the net QRS is negative in I and aVL and slightly positive in aVF, giving a frontal axis of about +175 degrees (rightward). QT 293 ms at RR 0.50 s gives QTc 416 ms. The previous tracing 106516875, recorded 13 hours earlier the same day, had a markedly wide QRS of 152 ms with a tall broad R wave in V1 and a wide terminal negativity in I and V6, i.e. a right bundle branch block pattern; that wide QRS has resolved on the present tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular RR 0.94-0.98 s, consistent P waves with PR 174 ms. QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +66 degrees. The QT is markedly prolonged at about 520 ms and, at RR 0.96 s, the Bazett QTc is about 529 ms (tight agreement across leads), above the 500 ms watch-list threshold. This tracing was obtained on 2025-11-24, two weeks after amiodarone was started. The previous ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07, sinus bradycardia 47/min) had a QTc of 404 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms since amiodarone was begun.

Atrial fibrillation: the ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR 0.41-1.07 s, coefficient of variation 0.28) and there is no reproducible atrial deflection before the QRS complexes (beat-to-beat correlation of the pre-QRS segment only 0.03), so no PR interval can be measured. Mean ventricular rate about 99/min. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis -51 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 327 ms at a median RR of 0.61 s gives QTc 420 ms. This is the only tracing in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison. The patient carries a diagnosis of atrial fibrillation and is anticoagulated with warfarin.

80-year-old woman whose cardiology clinic notes (most recently 2026-05-28) document persistent atrial fibrillation. Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg only; no anticoagulant order is active as of 2026-09-24, and aspirin is not a substitute for anticoagulation in AF. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: congestive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure) 1, hypertension 1, age 75 or older 2, type 2 diabetes mellitus 1, prior cerebral infarction/TIA with residual deficits 2, vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis) 1, female sex 1. Oral anticoagulation is strongly recommended; needs review.

48-year-old man whose cardiology clinic notes (most recently 2026-06-12) document paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; the chart also carries 'other specified cardiac dysrhythmias' and prior long-term anticoagulant use. Only famotidine and pantoprazole are current, so no anticoagulant is in place. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure - congestive heart failure unspecified, acute systolic heart failure and other primary cardiomyopathies documented in the chart - 1, plus hypertension 1). A score of 2 or more in a man meets the guideline recommendation for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of anticoagulation needs review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 2026-08-20 (valid through 2026-12-28) and is current. The 2026-08-12 summary of outside records documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 and 2 units transfused, and states that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. The clinic restarted apixaban (and continued aspirin plus clopidogrel) at the 2026-08-20 visit without any documented reconsideration of that recommendation. A current anticoagulant despite a documented recent major GI bleed and an explicit instruction to hold pending review needs prescriber review.

At the 2026-07-15 cardiology visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started. Rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was ordered at the same visit and was never stopped: both orders are active as of 2026-09-24 (rivaroxaban valid to 2026-12-25, apixaban to 2026-12-26) and the 2026-07-15 medication list itself shows both drugs. Two concurrent oral anticoagulants create a major bleeding hazard, particularly in a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and thrombocytopenia. Needs immediate reconciliation.

The 2026-06-10 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm with no consistent P waves at a ventricular rate of about 140/min, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same atrial fibrillation with a rate of about 144/min. The documented rhythm and rate are therefore both inconsistent with the same-day tracings, and the discrepancy needs clinical review (this patient is on warfarin for pulmonary embolism, and unrecognised rapid AF changes rate-control and anticoagulation decisions).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) is current, most recently ordered 2026-04-23 and valid through 2027-01-02. The patient's most recent ECG is 108018814 (2023-10-08): sinus rhythm at 68/min, RR 0.88 s, QT about 480 ms, Bazett QTc about 512 ms, which meets the clinic threshold of 500 ms or more and requires prescriber review. Note that the 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this same tracing as 'QT acceptable'. A repeat ECG on therapy plus review of the need for escitalopram is required.

interpretations.explanation: Recorded at the 2026-03-07 cardiology visit, 5 days after citalopram was started. Regular P wave before every QRS with an upright P in II and a normal PR; RR 0.66-0.86 s with mild respiratory variation. Narrow QRS, normal precordial progression, no bundle branch block and no AV block. QT 330 ms at RR 0.74 s gives a Bazett QTc of 382 ms, well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. No prior tracing for comparison. The note for that visit describing 'sinus rhythm' agrees with the tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular RR 0.57-0.59 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS and PR about 194 ms (upper normal). QRS 98 ms - slightly prolonged but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block is coded; the ST-T complex is broad and the repolarisation abnormal. QT about 323 ms at RR 0.58 s gives QTc 424 ms. The previous tracing 100698634 (2025-06-20) showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with QTc 388 ms; the rate has fallen but rhythm, conduction and QTc are otherwise unchanged (QTc change 36 ms, below the 60 ms threshold).

Sinus tachycardia at 109/min. The RR intervals are regular (0.54-0.62 s, coefficient of variation 0.03) and a low amplitude P wave precedes each QRS with PR about 136 ms; the baseline is noisy, which reduces beat-to-beat P wave correlation, but the rhythm is regular and atrially driven. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +45 degrees. QT 321 ms at RR 0.55 s gives QTc 433 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: RR intervals range from 0.35 to 0.65 s and are irregularly irregular (coefficient of variation 0.16), with no organised atrial activity before the QRS complexes (pre-QRS beat-to-beat correlation 0.40, no measurable P wave), so no PR interval can be given. Mean ventricular rate about 144/min. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about -2 degrees. QT 289 ms at a median RR of 0.42 s gives QTc 447 ms. The preceding tracing 107914094, taken 2 hours earlier the same day, shows the same atrial fibrillation at about 140/min, so there is no change between them. Both tracings contradict the 2026-06-10 clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'.

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular RR 0.86-0.88 s, consistent P waves with PR 152 ms. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis -24 degrees, within the normal range. QT 406 ms at RR 0.87 s gives QTc 435 ms. The previous tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27, sinus 60/min, QTc 402 ms) shows the same rhythm and conduction; the QTc change of 33 ms is below the 60 ms threshold, so there are no coded changes.

Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular RR 0.60-0.63 s, with a small upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and a short PR of about 100-105 ms. QRS 74 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis -12 degrees. QT 294 ms at RR 0.62 s gives QTc 375 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular RR 0.82-0.84 s, consistent P waves with PR 138 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block, axis +22 degrees. QT 373 ms at RR 0.83 s gives QTc 409 ms, below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. This is the only ECG in the chart and it predates the start of escitalopram on 2026-08-01, so no prior comparison is possible and a post-start tracing is still required.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.70, 1.13, 1.15, 1.17, 0.74, 0.91, 0.70 s; coefficient of variation 0.20) and no organised P wave can be identified before the QRS complexes (pre-QRS amplitude 0.024 mV with beat-to-beat correlation only 0.63), so no PR interval is reported. Mean ventricular rate about 53/min. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +25 degrees. QT 442 ms at a median RR of 1.13 s gives QTc 415 ms. The previous tracing 107873952, only three days earlier (2024-11-12), showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with a clear P wave and PR 176 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation. The patient is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min, regular RR 0.98-1.08 s, with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and a short PR of about 94 ms. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +59 degrees. QT 429 ms at RR 1.04 s gives QTc 423 ms. The previous tracing 106045460 from the day before (2025-03-08, sinus 62/min, PR 96 ms, QTc 455 ms) is essentially the same; the QTc change of 32 ms is below the 60 ms threshold. Note that this tracing long predates the haloperidol started on 2026-09-15, for which a new ECG is due.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular RR 0.72-0.73 s, consistent P waves with PR 140 ms. QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block, axis +51 degrees. QT 343 ms at RR 0.72 s gives QTc 404 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77/min, regular RR 0.77-0.80 s, with a prominent consistent P wave and PR 154 ms. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +64 degrees. QT 399 ms at RR 0.78 s gives QTc 451 ms. The previous tracing 109048192 (2020-02-02) was also sinus at 75/min but with a much longer QT, giving a QTc of about 528 ms; the QTc has therefore fallen by more than 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min with a consistent P wave preceding each QRS (P wave consistency 0.97) and regular RR intervals of 0.50 s. Narrow QRS at 92 ms, no bundle branch block, PR 192 ms is at the upper limit of normal but not first degree block. QT 285 ms with RR 0.50 s gives QTc 403 ms. Compared with the previous tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 94 ms, QTc 398 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus bradycardia at 54/min, regular RR 1.07-1.12 s, with a consistent P wave before every QRS. The PR interval is prolonged at about 214 ms, i.e. first degree AV block, with 1:1 conduction. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +13 degrees. QT 396 ms at RR 1.11 s gives QTc 378 ms. The previous tracing 103042067 (2024-11-30, sinus 51/min, PR about 188 ms, QTc 359 ms) showed the same rhythm and no bundle branch block; PR has lengthened slightly but none of the coded change categories apply (QTc change 19 ms).

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. RR intervals vary chaotically from 0.29 to 0.58 s (coefficient of variation 0.19) with no reproducible atrial deflection before the QRS complexes (pre-QRS beat-to-beat correlation 0.17), so no PR interval can be measured. The previous tracing 107374881 from the evening before (2025-09-12) showed a regular sinus rhythm at about 77/min (RR 0.77-0.79 s) with a single premature beat, so this tracing represents new atrial fibrillation; amiodarone was started the same morning and the patient is now on apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at 73/min, RR 0.79-0.92 s, with a prominent consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 168 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +9 degrees. QT 358 ms at RR 0.83 s gives QTc 396 ms. The previous tracing 105362569 (2025-11-21, sinus 67/min) had a QT of about 499 ms and a QTc of about 529 ms, so the QTc has decreased by more than 60 ms. The 2025-11-23 note describing 'ECG today: sinus rhythm' is consistent with this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular RR 0.80-0.82 s, with a clear P wave before each QRS and PR about 184 ms (upper normal, not first degree block). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +57 degrees. QT 377 ms at RR 0.81 s gives QTc 419 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, RR 0.54 s and perfectly regular, with a clear consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 164 ms - no evidence of atrial flutter despite the coded history of flutter. QRS 94 ms; deep S in V1 and tall R in V6 but no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees. QT 274 ms at RR 0.54 s gives QTc 374 ms. The previous tracing 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus tachycardia 115/min, QTc 383 ms) is unchanged in rhythm, conduction and QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 61/min with a single premature beat: RR intervals are 0.98, 0.99, 0.54 (premature), 1.39 (post-extrasystolic pause), then 0.98, 0.97, 0.95, 0.96, 0.98 s, and a consistent P wave precedes the sinus beats (beat-to-beat correlation 0.94). The underlying rhythm is therefore sinus, not atrial fibrillation, although the chart documents paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. PR about 200 ms, at the upper limit of normal. QRS 102 ms - mildly prolonged but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block is coded. Frontal axis -31 degrees, i.e. borderline left axis deviation. QT 365 ms at a median RR of 0.97 s gives QTc 370 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular RR 0.86-0.90 s with a consistent upright P wave and normal PR. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +46 degrees. The T waves are broad and late: QT is about 480 ms and, at RR 0.88 s, the Bazett QTc is about 512 ms (tangent method, consistent across leads I, II, V2-V6), i.e. above the 500 ms clinic threshold. The previous tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23) had QTc 357 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. This patient is on escitalopram, and the 2024-05-14 note that started it described this tracing as 'QT acceptable'; the measured QTc does not support that.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 0.49-0.50 s and perfectly regular, with a low amplitude but consistent P wave before every QRS. PR 172 ms, QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +59 degrees. QT 281 ms at RR 0.50 s gives QTc 399 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 101/min with regular RR intervals and a clear P wave before each QRS (PR 132 ms). QRS 90 ms with normal precordial progression and no conduction block; axis +58 degrees. QT 312 ms at RR 0.59 s gives QTc 405 ms. The immediately preceding tracing 102910502 was taken 34 seconds earlier on the same day and is essentially identical (sinus 101/min, QRS 90 ms, QTc 401 ms), so there are no changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, RR 1.14-1.18 s and regular, with a small but consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 166 ms. QRS 92 ms; large precordial voltages with deep S in V1 and tall R in V6, but no bundle branch block. Axis +34 degrees. QT 431 ms at RR 1.16 s gives QTc 400 ms. Compared with 104629882 (2023-05-22, sinus 57/min with an occasional premature beat, QTc 369 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (change 31 ms).

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 0.49-0.50 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 132 ms). The QRS is now narrow at 82 ms. QRS voltages are low; the net QRS is negative in I and aVL and slightly positive in aVF, giving a frontal axis of about +175 degrees (rightward). QT 293 ms at RR 0.50 s gives QTc 416 ms. The previous tracing 106516875, recorded 13 hours earlier the same day, had a markedly wide QRS of 152 ms with a tall broad R wave in V1 and a wide terminal negativity in I and V6, i.e. a right bundle branch block pattern; that wide QRS has resolved on the present tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular RR 0.94-0.98 s, consistent P waves with PR 174 ms. QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +66 degrees. The QT is markedly prolonged at about 520 ms and, at RR 0.96 s, the Bazett QTc is about 529 ms (tight agreement across leads), above the 500 ms watch-list threshold. This tracing was obtained on 2025-11-24, two weeks after amiodarone was started. The previous ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07, sinus bradycardia 47/min) had a QTc of 404 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms since amiodarone was begun.

Atrial fibrillation: the ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR 0.41-1.07 s, coefficient of variation 0.28) and there is no reproducible atrial deflection before the QRS complexes (beat-to-beat correlation of the pre-QRS segment only 0.03), so no PR interval can be measured. Mean ventricular rate about 99/min. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis -51 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 327 ms at a median RR of 0.61 s gives QTc 420 ms. This is the only tracing in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison. The patient carries a diagnosis of atrial fibrillation and is anticoagulated with warfarin.

INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was completed within the required time.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: congestive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure) 1, hypertension 1, age 75 or older 2, type 2 diabetes mellitus 1, prior cerebral infarction/TIA with residual deficits 2, vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis) 1, female sex 1. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure - congestive heart failure unspecified, acute systolic heart failure and other primary cardiomyopathies documented in the chart - 1, plus hypertension 1). A score of 2 or more in a man meets the guideline recommendation for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of anticoagulation needs review.

The clinic restarted apixaban (and continued aspirin plus clopidogrel) at the 2026-08-20 visit without any documented reconsideration of that recommendation. A current anticoagulant despite a documented recent major GI bleed and an explicit instruction to hold pending review needs prescriber review.

Rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was ordered at the same visit and was never stopped: both orders are active as of 2026-09-24 (rivaroxaban valid to 2026-12-25, apixaban to 2026-12-26) and the 2026-07-15 medication list itself shows both drugs. Two concurrent oral anticoagulants create a major bleeding hazard, particularly in a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and thrombocytopenia. Needs immediate reconciliation.

Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm with no consistent P waves at a ventricular rate of about 140/min, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same atrial fibrillation with a rate of about 144/min. The documented rhythm and rate are therefore both inconsistent with the same-day tracings, and the discrepancy needs clinical review (this patient is on warfarin for pulmonary embolism, and unrecognised rapid AF changes rate-control and anticoagulation decisions).

Most recent electrolytes are potassium 4.1 mmol/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 2025-08-23), so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. A repeat ECG on therapy plus review of the need for escitalopram is required.

The patient is also on warfarin, so any amiodarone dose change will need INR follow-up. Prescriber review of continued amiodarone and a repeat ECG are required.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min with a consistent P wave preceding each QRS (P wave consistency 0.97) and regular RR intervals of 0.50 s. interpretations.explanation: Recorded at the 2026-03-07 cardiology visit, 5 days after citalopram was started. Regular P wave before every QRS with an upright P in II and a normal PR; RR 0.66-0.86 s with mild respiratory variation. Narrow QRS, normal precordial progression, no bundle branch block and no AV block. QT 330 ms at RR 0.74 s gives a Bazett QTc of 382 ms, well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. No prior tracing for comparison. The note for that visit describing 'sinus rhythm' agrees with the tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular RR 0.57-0.59 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS and PR about 194 ms (upper normal). QRS 98 ms - slightly prolonged but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block is coded; the ST-T complex is broad and the repolarisation abnormal. QT about 323 ms at RR 0.58 s gives QTc 424 ms. The previous tracing 100698634 (2025-06-20) showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with QTc 388 ms; the rate has fallen but rhythm, conduction and QTc are otherwise unchanged (QTc change 36 ms, below the 60 ms threshold).

Sinus tachycardia at 109/min. The RR intervals are regular (0.54-0.62 s, coefficient of variation 0.03) and a low amplitude P wave precedes each QRS with PR about 136 ms; the baseline is noisy, which reduces beat-to-beat P wave correlation, but the rhythm is regular and atrially driven. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +45 degrees. QT 321 ms at RR 0.55 s gives QTc 433 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: RR intervals range from 0.35 to 0.65 s and are irregularly irregular (coefficient of variation 0.16), with no organised atrial activity before the QRS complexes (pre-QRS beat-to-beat correlation 0.40, no measurable P wave), so no PR interval can be given. Mean ventricular rate about 144/min. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about -2 degrees. QT 289 ms at a median RR of 0.42 s gives QTc 447 ms. The preceding tracing 107914094, taken 2 hours earlier the same day, shows the same atrial fibrillation at about 140/min, so there is no change between them. Both tracings contradict the 2026-06-10 clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'.

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular RR 0.86-0.88 s, consistent P waves with PR 152 ms. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis -24 degrees, within the normal range. The previous tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27, sinus 60/min, QTc 402 ms) shows the same rhythm and conduction; the QTc change of 33 ms is below the 60 ms threshold, so there are no coded changes.

Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular RR 0.60-0.63 s, with a small upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and a short PR of about 100-105 ms. Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular RR 0.82-0.84 s, consistent P waves with PR 138 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block, axis +22 degrees. This is the only ECG in the chart and it predates the start of escitalopram on 2026-08-01, so no prior comparison is possible and a post-start tracing is still required.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular RR 0.72-0.73 s, consistent P waves with PR 140 ms. QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block, axis +51 degrees. QT 343 ms at RR 0.72 s gives QTc 404 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. The 2025-11-23 note describing 'ECG today: sinus rhythm' is consistent with this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular RR 0.80-0.82 s, with a clear P wave before each QRS and PR about 184 ms (upper normal, not first degree block). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +57 degrees. QT 377 ms at RR 0.81 s gives QTc 419 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, RR 0.54 s and perfectly regular, with a clear consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 164 ms - no evidence of atrial flutter despite the coded history of flutter. QRS 94 ms; deep S in V1 and tall R in V6 but no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees. QT 274 ms at RR 0.54 s gives QTc 374 ms. The previous tracing 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus tachycardia 115/min, QTc 383 ms) is unchanged in rhythm, conduction and QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 61/min with a single premature beat: RR intervals are 0.98, 0.99, 0.54 (premature), 1.39 (post-extrasystolic pause), then 0.98, 0.97, 0.95, 0.96, 0.98 s, and a consistent P wave precedes the sinus beats (beat-to-beat correlation 0.94). The underlying rhythm is therefore sinus, not atrial fibrillation, although the chart documents paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. PR about 200 ms, at the upper limit of normal. QRS 102 ms - mildly prolonged but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block is coded. Frontal axis -31 degrees, i.e. borderline left axis deviation. QT 365 ms at a median RR of 0.97 s gives QTc 370 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular RR 0.84-0.88 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 142 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block. The frontal plane QRS is dominantly negative in I and aVL and close to isoelectric but slightly negative in aVF with a positive net QRS in III, giving a frontal axis of about -173 degrees, i.e. an extreme (north-west) axis. QT 353 ms at RR 0.86 s gives QTc 379 ms, comfortably below the 500 ms watch-list threshold for his escitalopram. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison; it was obtained on 2026-04-29, outside the 14-day window after escitalopram was started on 2026-04-10.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, RR 0.80-0.89 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS and PR about 152 ms. Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular RR 0.86-0.91 s, with a prominent P wave before each QRS and PR 140 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +47 degrees. Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular RR 0.86-0.90 s with a consistent upright P wave and normal PR. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +46 degrees. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 0.49-0.50 s and perfectly regular, with a low amplitude but consistent P wave before every QRS. PR 172 ms, QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +59 degrees. QT 281 ms at RR 0.50 s gives QTc 399 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 101/min with regular RR intervals and a clear P wave before each QRS (PR 132 ms). QRS 90 ms with normal precordial progression and no conduction block; axis +58 degrees. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 0.49-0.50 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 132 ms). The QRS is now narrow at 82 ms. QRS voltages are low; the net QRS is negative in I and aVL and slightly positive in aVF, giving a frontal axis of about +175 degrees (rightward). QT 293 ms at RR 0.50 s gives QTc 416 ms. The previous tracing 106516875, recorded 13 hours earlier the same day, had a markedly wide QRS of 152 ms with a tall broad R wave in V1 and a wide terminal negativity in I and V6, i.e. a right bundle branch block pattern; that wide QRS has resolved on the present tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular RR 0.94-0.98 s, consistent P waves with PR 174 ms. QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +66 degrees. The QT is markedly prolonged at about 520 ms and, at RR 0.96 s, the Bazett QTc is about 529 ms (tight agreement across leads), above the 500 ms watch-list threshold. This tracing was obtained on 2025-11-24, two weeks after amiodarone was started. The previous ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07, sinus bradycardia 47/min) had a QTc of 404 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms since amiodarone was begun.

Atrial fibrillation: the ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR 0.41-1.07 s, coefficient of variation 0.28) and there is no reproducible atrial deflection before the QRS complexes (beat-to-beat correlation of the pre-QRS segment only 0.03), so no PR interval can be measured. Mean ventricular rate about 99/min. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis -51 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 327 ms at a median RR of 0.61 s gives QTc 420 ms. This is the only tracing in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison. The patient carries a diagnosis of atrial fibrillation and is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Two concurrent oral anticoagulants create a major bleeding hazard, particularly in a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and thrombocytopenia. Needs immediate reconciliation.

The 2026-06-10 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm with no consistent P waves at a ventricular rate of about 140/min, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same atrial fibrillation with a rate of about 144/min. The documented rhythm and rate are therefore both inconsistent with the same-day tracings, and the discrepancy needs clinical review (this patient is on warfarin for pulmonary embolism, and unrecognised rapid AF changes rate-control and anticoagulation decisions).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) is current, most recently ordered 2026-04-23 and valid through 2027-01-02. interpretations.explanation: Recorded at the 2026-03-07 cardiology visit, 5 days after citalopram was started. Regular P wave before every QRS with an upright P in II and a normal PR; RR 0.66-0.86 s with mild respiratory variation. Narrow QRS, normal precordial progression, no bundle branch block and no AV block. QT 330 ms at RR 0.74 s gives a Bazett QTc of 382 ms, well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. No prior tracing for comparison. The note for that visit describing 'sinus rhythm' agrees with the tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular RR 0.57-0.59 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS and PR about 194 ms (upper normal). QRS 98 ms - slightly prolonged but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block is coded; the ST-T complex is broad and the repolarisation abnormal. QT about 323 ms at RR 0.58 s gives QTc 424 ms. The previous tracing 100698634 (2025-06-20) showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with QTc 388 ms; the rate has fallen but rhythm, conduction and QTc are otherwise unchanged (QTc change 36 ms, below the 60 ms threshold).

Sinus tachycardia at 109/min. The RR intervals are regular (0.54-0.62 s, coefficient of variation 0.03) and a low amplitude P wave precedes each QRS with PR about 136 ms; the baseline is noisy, which reduces beat-to-beat P wave correlation, but the rhythm is regular and atrially driven. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +45 degrees. QT 321 ms at RR 0.55 s gives QTc 433 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: RR intervals range from 0.35 to 0.65 s and are irregularly irregular (coefficient of variation 0.16), with no organised atrial activity before the QRS complexes (pre-QRS beat-to-beat correlation 0.40, no measurable P wave), so no PR interval can be given. Mean ventricular rate about 144/min. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about -2 degrees. QT 289 ms at a median RR of 0.42 s gives QTc 447 ms. The preceding tracing 107914094, taken 2 hours earlier the same day, shows the same atrial fibrillation at about 140/min, so there is no change between them. Both tracings contradict the 2026-06-10 clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'.

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular RR 0.86-0.88 s, consistent P waves with PR 152 ms. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis -24 degrees, within the normal range. The previous tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27, sinus 60/min, QTc 402 ms) shows the same rhythm and conduction; the QTc change of 33 ms is below the 60 ms threshold, so there are no coded changes.

Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular RR 0.60-0.63 s, with a small upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and a short PR of about 100-105 ms. Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular RR 0.82-0.84 s, consistent P waves with PR 138 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block, axis +22 degrees. This is the only ECG in the chart and it predates the start of escitalopram on 2026-08-01, so no prior comparison is possible and a post-start tracing is still required.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response. The patient is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular RR 0.72-0.73 s, consistent P waves with PR 140 ms. QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block, axis +51 degrees. QT 343 ms at RR 0.72 s gives QTc 404 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular RR 0.80-0.82 s, with a clear P wave before each QRS and PR about 184 ms (upper normal, not first degree block). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +57 degrees. The previous tracing 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus tachycardia 115/min, QTc 383 ms) is unchanged in rhythm, conduction and QTc.

The underlying rhythm is therefore sinus, not atrial fibrillation, although the chart documents paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. PR about 200 ms, at the upper limit of normal. QRS 102 ms - mildly prolonged but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block is coded. Frontal axis -31 degrees, i.e. borderline left axis deviation. QT 365 ms at a median RR of 0.97 s gives QTc 370 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular RR 0.84-0.88 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 142 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block. The frontal plane QRS is dominantly negative in I and aVL and close to isoelectric but slightly negative in aVF with a positive net QRS in III, giving a frontal axis of about -173 degrees, i.e. an extreme (north-west) axis. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior for comparison; it was obtained on 2026-04-29, outside the 14-day window after escitalopram was started on 2026-04-10.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, RR 0.80-0.89 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS and PR about 152 ms. The previous tracing 107149156 (2020-06-17, sinus tachycardia 132/min) had a QTc of about 444 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular RR 0.86-0.91 s, with a prominent P wave before each QRS and PR 140 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +47 degrees. Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular RR 1.11-1.17 s, with a prominent consistent P wave and PR 174 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -9 degrees. QT 383 ms at RR 1.14 s gives QTc 359 ms. Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular RR 0.86-0.90 s with a consistent upright P wave and normal PR. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +46 degrees. The T waves are broad and late: QT is about 480 ms and, at RR 0.88 s, the Bazett QTc is about 512 ms (tangent method, consistent across leads I, II, V2-V6), i.e. above the 500 ms clinic threshold. The previous tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23) had QTc 357 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. This patient is on escitalopram, and the 2024-05-14 note that started it described this tracing as 'QT acceptable'; the measured QTc does not support that.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 0.49-0.50 s and perfectly regular, with a low amplitude but consistent P wave before every QRS. PR 172 ms, QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +59 degrees. QT 281 ms at RR 0.50 s gives QTc 399 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 101/min with regular RR intervals and a clear P wave before each QRS (PR 132 ms). QRS 90 ms with normal precordial progression and no conduction block; axis +58 degrees. QT 312 ms at RR 0.59 s gives QTc 405 ms. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, RR 1.14-1.18 s and regular, with a small but consistent P wave before each QRS and PR 166 ms. Compared with 104629882 (2023-05-22, sinus 57/min with an occasional premature beat, QTc 369 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (change 31 ms).

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, RR 0.49-0.50 s, with a consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 132 ms). The QRS is now narrow at 82 ms. QRS voltages are low; the net QRS is negative in I and aVL and slightly positive in aVF, giving a frontal axis of about +175 degrees (rightward). QT 293 ms at RR 0.50 s gives QTc 416 ms. The previous tracing 106516875, recorded 13 hours earlier the same day, had a markedly wide QRS of 152 ms with a tall broad R wave in V1 and a wide terminal negativity in I and V6, i.e. a right bundle branch block pattern; that wide QRS has resolved on the present tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular RR 0.94-0.98 s, consistent P waves with PR 174 ms. QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +66 degrees. The QT is markedly prolonged at about 520 ms and, at RR 0.96 s, the Bazett QTc is about 529 ms (tight agreement across leads), above the 500 ms watch-list threshold. This tracing was obtained on 2025-11-24, two weeks after amiodarone was started. The previous ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07, sinus bradycardia 47/min) had a QTc of 404 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms since amiodarone was begun.

QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about -2 degrees. QT 268 ms at RR 0.43 s gives QTc 410 ms. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm with no consistent P waves at a ventricular rate of about 140/min, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same atrial fibrillation with a rate of about 144/min. The documented rhythm and rate are therefore both inconsistent with the same-day tracings, and the discrepancy needs clinical review (this patient is on warfarin for pulmonary embolism, and unrecognised rapid AF changes rate-control and anticoagulation decisions).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) is current, most recently ordered 2026-04-23 and valid through 2027-01-02. The patient's most recent ECG is 108018814 (2023-10-08): sinus rhythm at 68/min, RR 0.88 s, QT about 480 ms, Bazett QTc about 512 ms, which meets the clinic threshold of 500 ms or more and requires prescriber review. Most recent electrolytes are potassium 4.1 mmol/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 2025-08-23), so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. A repeat ECG on therapy plus review of the need for escitalopram is required.

The most recent ECG is 106885519 (2025-11-24), obtained two weeks after amiodarone was started: sinus rhythm at 62/min, RR 0.96 s, QT about 520 ms, Bazett QTc about 529 ms, at or above the clinic 500 ms threshold. interpretations.explanation: Recorded at the 2026-03-07 cardiology visit, 5 days after citalopram was started. Narrow QRS, normal precordial progression, no bundle branch block and no AV block. QT 330 ms at RR 0.74 s gives a Bazett QTc of 382 ms, well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. No prior tracing for comparison. The note for that visit describing 'sinus rhythm' agrees with the tracing.

A score of 2 or more in a man meets the guideline recommendation for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of anticoagulation needs review.

The clinic restarted apixaban (and continued aspirin plus clopidogrel) at the 2026-08-20 visit without any documented reconsideration of that recommendation. A current anticoagulant despite a documented recent major GI bleed and an explicit instruction to hold pending review needs prescriber review.

Two concurrent oral anticoagulants create a major bleeding hazard, particularly in a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and thrombocytopenia. Needs immediate reconciliation.

Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm with no consistent P waves at a ventricular rate of about 140/min, and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same atrial fibrillation with a rate of about 144/min. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was completed within the required time.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (Condition 427.31, also carried in every clinic note). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery as vascular disease 1); for a man a score of 2 or more carries a guideline recommendation for oral anticoagulation. The historical code 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is remote and is not documented as an active bleeding contraindication. Needs review for initiation of oral anticoagulation.

The requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old woman on warfarin plus amiodarone.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: congestive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure) 1, hypertension 1, age 75 or older 2, type 2 diabetes mellitus 1, prior cerebral infarction/TIA with residual deficits 2, vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis) 1, female sex 1. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure - congestive heart failure unspecified, acute systolic heart failure and other primary cardiomyopathies documented in the chart - 1, plus hypertension 1). A score of 2 or more in a man meets the guideline recommendation for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of anticoagulation needs review.

The clinic restarted apixaban (and continued aspirin plus clopidogrel) at the 2026-08-20 visit without any documented reconsideration of that recommendation. A current anticoagulant despite a documented recent major GI bleed and an explicit instruction to hold pending review needs prescriber review.

Two concurrent oral anticoagulants create a major bleeding hazard, particularly in a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and thrombocytopenia. Needs immediate reconciliation.
